text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary error rate spike detected for service `redwood-api` (canary id: canary-2026-03-15). Error rate 5xx > 12% over 3m, latency p95 up 2.6x. Automated rollback did NOT trigger (threshold not met due to anomaly filter). Paging oncall @maya, @sam.

maya: I'm on it. pulling up dashboards now. can someone paste the canary config? which traffic percentage was sent to canary?

sam: Canary was at 10% traffic, 200rps. New model quantized build v2.3.8 rolled 11:42 UTC. Checking logs for error class.

rajesh: Error pattern looks like OOM-ish on a subset of GPU nodes — `CUDA OOM` in the worker logs, plus `kv-cache` eviction logs. Might be an arg parsing change in runtime. Not sure if it hits all replicas.

liz: FYI automated rollback policy is `>15% 5xx for 5m` — we hit 12% for 3m so it didn't fire. I'm escalating to infra but we should consider manual rollback/kill-switch.

maya: Customer impact? product-ops?

product-ops: Early telemetry from production: chat API error increase for ~8% of active sessions for customers on us-east region. No billing anomalies yet. A few support tickets: 3 reports from one mid-market customer about timeouts. We're drafting a short status note.

sam: Given the OOM hints, I recommend immediate feature-flag kill and manual rollback of canary. Sequence: 1) flip FF to block new requests to model v2.3.8, 2) scale canary down/out, or 3) rollback to previous canary image v2.3.6, 4) run smoke tests, 5) promote safe revision.

rajesh: Agree. Also capture core dumps / stack traces — add `--retain-logs` on the failing nodes to investigation.

devops-bot: Executing: `featureflag set redwood.model.router allow_v2_3_8 false --env prod --region us-east` (requested by @sam).

sam: I toggled the flag. Confirmed new requests are routed to fallback models. Can we start rollback to stable now? I'll run the rollback with the deployment tool.

maya: Copy. @liz can you update the deploy-safety channel with rollback start and ETA? Also notify support to pause outbound notifications until we confirm stability.

liz: Posting now. ETA 15min for rollback + smoke. Support notified to pause customer notifications and to triage existing tickets.

sam: Rolling back deployment: `redwoodctl rollout undo redwood-api --to-revision=2026031501 --namespace=prod --wait`

sam: Output: ```
Starting rollback to revision 2026031501
Scaling canary pods to 0
Updating service routing
Waiting for stable rollout...
Rollout complete: stable at revision 2026031501
```

maya: Can you run the smoke test suite? quick sanity checks: 1) chat generation baseline 2) health-check endpoints 3) embedding route at 1qps for 2m

sam: Running smoke: `./scripts/smoke.sh --targets chat,embed,health --region us-east --duration 2m`

sam: Smoke results: chat OK (latency p95 back to 180ms), embedding OK, health checks passing. No 5xx observed in last 2m.

rajesh: Checking infra metrics — node memory usage trending down on the previously affected hosts. KV-cache evictions stop after rollback. Looks clean.

product-ops: Customer impact assessment: ~8% sessions briefly affected, most retries succeeded after a few seconds. We're recommending owner outreach to the 3 customers with tickets. Draft message in #support-drafts for review.

maya: Good. We'll keep canary disabled for now until we patch the runtime and run a controlled bake. @sam please collect the failing pod logs (with timestamps) and upload to the incident artifact store.

sam: Logs collected and uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/1993456789/logs.tar.gz. Included stack traces and OOM messages.

liz: Filing followup: create a postmortem doc and assign action items. I'll create the incident PM and link the rollback timeline.

rajesh: Short-term action: revert quantization change in runtime branch, add more conservative memory limits on canary nodes, and update the automated rollback threshold from `15% 5xx 5m` to `12% 5xx 3m` for canary policy until we stabilize. We'll propose in change review.

devops-bot: Incident runbook update: `canary-rollback-threshold` draft pushed to repo at `infra/runbooks/canary-rollback.md` (PR #412).

product-ops: Sending customer comms to the affected accounts, will send postmortem blurb after internal review.

maya: Handoff: I'm going to hand oncall to @sam for follow-up investigation and postmortem. If anything regresses, page SRE2. Next oncall shift @sam starting now.

sam: Taking over. I'll coordinate the patch and schedule a controlled re-release once we have a fix and an improved rollback trigger. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup: 

devops-bot: Incident closed in channel. Please fill out postmortem template: `/incident create 1993456789 --severity P1 --impact customers-brief-failed-requests --owner sam`

maya: Marking as resolved in Slack. Follow-ups in the postmortem.

product-ops: Confirmed support outreach sent and accepted. We'll monitor for 24h and reopen if anomalies reappear.

sam: I'll post the root-cause summary and timeline in the postmortem doc later today.

liz: Thanks all, nice quick coordination. :rocket:
